questions.q: A backup file passes RESTORE VERIFYONLY with no errors. Does that guarantee it will restore successfully in a real disaster?
options: No — VERIFYONLY only checks the backup set's structure and completeness, not that a full restore will succeed without error
Yes — VERIFYONLY performs a complete real restore internally to confirm it
Yes, but only for full backups, not for log backups
No — VERIFYONLY only works on backups taken in the last 24 hours
questions.explain: VERIFYONLY is a structural sanity check, not a substitute for actually restoring the backup.

questions.q: Does RESTORE VERIFYONLY write any data or log files during its check?
options: No — it reads and validates the backup file without restoring any data
Yes — it fully restores the database to a temporary location
Yes — it restores only the log file portion
It depends on whether WITH RECOVERY is specified
questions.explain: VERIFYONLY never writes data or log files — that's precisely why it's fast.

questions.q: Why does WITH CHECKSUM at backup time make RESTORE VERIFYONLY more useful?
options: It stores per-page checksums in the backup that VERIFYONLY can check against, catching corrupted pages
It compresses the backup so VERIFYONLY runs faster
It automatically schedules a test restore every night
It has no effect on VERIFYONLY at all
questions.explain: Without CHECKSUM at backup time, there's no stored per-page checksum for VERIFYONLY to validate page contents against.

questions.q: What is the only way to be truly certain a backup restores cleanly?
options: Actually restore it, ideally to a test instance on a regular schedule
Run RESTORE VERIFYONLY twice in a row
Check that the .bak file size matches the database size
Confirm the backup job in msdb shows a green checkmark
questions.explain: A genuine test restore is the only way to confirm a backup fully works — VERIFYONLY does not substitute for it.

questions.q: Which of these does RESTORE VERIFYONLY explicitly NOT confirm?
options: That the destination server has enough disk space for a real restore
That the backup header is intact
That the expected number of pages are present in the backup set
That the backup file can be read from start to finish
questions.explain: VERIFYONLY doesn't check destination disk space, because it never actually attempts to write restored files anywhere.
